summary: The @gyomu/approval-core package provides the foundational domain models, interfaces, and service definitions for managing approval workflows. It enables systems to track, evaluate, and audit requests that require manual or automated intervention. By decoupling business logic from persistence, it offers a standardized contract for lifecycle management and historical auditing.
responsibilities: Define the domain models for approval requests, decisions, and lifecycle states.
Specify the command interfaces for initiating, approving, and rejecting requests.
Establish architectural ports to decouple approval logic from infrastructure implementations.
Provide service abstractions for auditing and retrieving historical approval records.
Ensure consistent identity and context tracking across approval interactions.

capabilities.name: Approval Lifecycle Management
capabilities.description: Models and tracks the end-to-end status of approval requests from initiation through to final resolution.

capabilities.name: Decision Evaluation Framework
capabilities.description: Defines structured outcomes for approval policy checks, including requirements for further authorization or denial.

capabilities.name: Interaction Ports
capabilities.description: Provides standardized interface contracts for request submission and state persistence, enabling integration with various backends.

capabilities.name: Auditing and History
capabilities.description: Enables retrieval and management of historical events and approval records associated with users and tools.

capabilities.name: Command Input Schemas
capabilities.description: Standardizes the parameter structures required for consistent user and system interactions with approval workflows.

designDecisions: Uses a port-based architecture to separate domain business rules from external system interactions.
Employs union types and structured data models to represent distinct lifecycle phases and decision outcomes.
Centralizes command schemas to ensure traceability and consistency in request processing.
Maintains clear separation between historical record-keeping and current state management.
usageGuidance: Implement the provided port interfaces when integrating custom storage or notification backends.
Use the defined model types to build user interfaces that display request states and allow for approval or rejection actions.
Leverage the history service to provide users with audit logs of their past approval activity.
Extend the workflow by utilizing the existing request and decision schemas as the source of truth for all approval-related logic.
